unit.name: RAG pipeline and common retrieval improvements
unit.description: Defines RAG, walks through the query-answering pipeline with embeddings and vector databases, and introduces chunking and HyDE as improvements over vanilla retrieval.
unit.summary: RAG is introduced as a response to standalone LLM problems: limited context, difficulty finding facts in long contexts, knowledge cutoffs, hallucinations, and lack of sources [ts=2709s]. The core idea is to integrate external knowledge sources such as databases, documents, or APIs so answers can be more accurate, up to date, grounded, and developer-controllable without retraining the model [ts=2783s]. In the medical QA example, documents are embedded into lower-dimensional representations, stored in a vector database, and retrieved by comparing the embedded user query against document embeddings [ts=2831s]. The retrieved documents are added to the prompt with instructions such as answering only from the documents and saying "I don't know" when the answer is absent [ts=2955s]. The unit then covers chunking for large documents and HyDE, where the query is first expanded into a hypothetical document whose embedding may be closer to target documents [ts=3049s].

key_points.text: RAG addresses limited context, stale knowledge, hallucinations, and missing sources in standalone LLM use.
RAG integrates external knowledge sources such as databases, documents, and APIs without touching model weights.
A RAG pipeline embeds knowledge-base documents into vector representations and stores them for retrieval.
Retrieval compares the embedded user query to vector-database items using an embedding distance metric.
The retrieved documents are added to the user query through a prompt template to ground generation.
Chunking stores document-level and chapter-level vectors to improve precision and sourcing for large documents.
HyDE generates a hypothetical answer document from the query, embeds it, and retrieves documents using that embedding.

kp_catalog.name: RAG retrieval pipeline
kp_catalog.description: End-to-end retrieval-augmented generation workflow: embed documents, store vectors, embed query, retrieve relevant documents, augment the prompt, and generate grounded output.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: RAG is presented as a common interview topic and a major method for adding up-to-date, source-grounded context without retraining [ts=2694s].

kp_catalog.name: RAG chunking and HyDE
kp_catalog.description: Advanced retrieval improvements: storing smaller document chunks and generating hypothetical documents to improve query-document embedding match.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The instructor presents chunking and HyDE as examples of active RAG research rather than exhaustive methods, so they are important but not the whole RAG topic [ts=3049s].
